title: The Time-Asymmetry of Causation
version: PhilSci-Archive 4475, preprint deposited 1 Mar 2009 (dated Nov 2008); printed as ch. 20 of Beebee, Hitchcock, Menzies (eds), Oxford Handbook of Causation, OUP 2010, pp. 414-444, DOI 10.1093/oxfordhb/9780199279739.003.0021. Page numbers of the printed version not checked.
locators: Sec. 1.1-1.4 (Hume, physicalist constraint, hyperrealism); 2.1-2.2 (Lewis, Elga); 3 (AKL view; 3.1 web not tree; 3.2 Future Hypothesis); 4-5 (deliberation, Practical Relevance Constraint); 6.3 (interventionism); 6.4 (summary); notes 4 and 26
relevance: Opinionated survey by defenders of the perspectival view; best single open map of the field, including the strongest objections to the Past-Hypothesis route and to hyperrealism
assumptions: Authors hold the subjectivist/perspectival view; their claim of 'considerable consensus' that there is no intrinsic causal asymmetry is theirs, not neutral
conclusion: Authors' claims: Hume's conventionalism and hyperrealism both fail the Practical Relevance Constraint; the third-arrow (PH/statistical) route reduces to convention at micro level and cannot explain the asymmetry of deliberation (a Future Hypothesis would not block action on the future); the most promising route starts from epistemically characterised deliberation
open_questions: Whether a genealogy of causal concepts from epistemic deliberation can be completed (authors say it is not attempted)
Whether the objectivity given up is acceptable
limits: Read in full except the reference list (skimmed). Authors are partisans of one position; hyperrealist replies are not in the text

title: Statistical Mechanics and the Asymmetry of Counterfactual Dependence
version: Author's HTML version at Princeton; Philosophy of Science 68(3) Supplement, 2001, S313-S324, DOI 10.1086/392918 (PhilPapers lists year 2000 for the PSA meeting). Pagination of the print version not checked.
locators: Sec. 2 (Lewis's criteria, asymmetry of miracles); 3 (sensitivity to final conditions); 4 (no asymmetry of miracles); 5 (traces)
relevance: Standard objection to Lewis: with deterministic time-reversal-invariant laws and no Past Hypothesis, small convergence miracles are as available as small divergence miracles
assumptions: Newtonian-style deterministic dynamics; Boltzmannian phase-space measure; empirical claim that thermodynamically irreversible processes are sensitive to small changes in their end states
conclusion: Author's claim: in many ordinary cases the nearest world with the antecedent can be reached by a small miracle after the antecedent time, so Lewis's analysis does not yield the asymmetry of counterfactual dependence; the asymmetry of overdetermination is tied to the entropy asymmetry
proof_status: Informal physical argument, not a theorem; relies on an empirical sensitivity claim
open_questions: Whether the result generalises beyond strongly coupled irreversible processes
Whether adding the Past Hypothesis restores the asymmetry (Albert, Loewer say yes; Frisch disputes)
limits: Read in full. Same author's later views not checked

title: Causation and the Direction of Time (Chapter 14 of an online Tooley manuscript, 'Causation')
version: Author's home-page PDF, undated; retrieved 2026-11-12. Not identified with any printed chapter of Time, Tense, and Causation (OUP 1997) or Causation: A Realist Approach (1987); the text refers to 'Chapter 4' and 'Chapter 11' of its own manuscript
locators: Sec. 14.1 (four considerations) and 14.4.1 (analysis of simultaneity and temporal priority; principles R, S, T, U) read directly; 14.2-14.3 and 14.5-14.8 (substantivalism, circularity, objections, Mehlberg, summary) read through a summarising fetch tool and a search-engine excerpt only, wording unchecked
relevance: Primary statement of the causal theory of time: direction of time defined from direction of causation, which is taken as asymmetric and basic
assumptions: Causal relation is primitive and asymmetric; backward causation is logically impossible (argued in his Ch. 4, not read); non-relativistic total temporal order; rejection of Humean supervenience
conclusion: Author's claim: A is earlier than B iff a finite chain of causal and pure spatial links joins them with at least one causal link; simultaneity is spatial relatedness; time's direction is a pervasive fact independent of boundary conditions
proof_status: Philosophical analysis; derivation of formal properties is argued in prose
open_questions: Argument of Ch. 4 against backward causation not read
Transfer to relativistic spacetime: the account assumes absolute simultaneity
limits: Partial read as stated in locators; do not cite wording from sections not read directly

title: Reichenbach's Common Cause Principle
version: SEP, first published 13 Jan 2020; retrieved 2026-11-12
locators: Sec. 2 (principle), 3 (history), 4-5 (examples, counterexamples) read directly; 6 (Fork Asymmetry) and 7 (Causal Markov Condition) via summarising fetch tool
relevance: Secondary account of Reichenbach's fork asymmetry, its entropy analogy, objections (Horwich, Arntzenius) and the later switch to colliders for causal direction
conclusion: As surveyed: Reichenbach claimed forks are open to the future and not the past; Arntzenius argues deterministic reversible dynamics yields closed forks; modern causal modelling infers direction from colliders
open_questions: Primary Reichenbach and Arntzenius not read
limits: Secondary. Secs. 6-7 content relayed by a summariser, treat as lead
